entries.note: Opt-in Node bridge reads the active environment in process.
Mutation applies to the current run; it is not persisted to the environment file.
Unset and clear are returned as explicit session changes; replaceIn uses visible scopes.
Opt-in Node bridge reads collection variables.
Collection mutations are session-scoped and carried back through the Rust contract.
Global mutations are session-scoped and are not persisted to a global file.
Runner iteration data is read-only and participates in visible variable precedence.
Runtime session mutations and request header changes are supported; broader scope semantics remain limited.
Postman-shaped URL host/path/query access, method, headers, cookies and raw/JSON/form body facades are supported; broader URL object parity remains limited.
Status, timing, raw text/body, JSON, header/cookie access, header value matching, jsonBody path checks and header/cookie toObject helpers are exposed.
Assertions are collected and affect runner/send exit status when scripts are enabled.
Equality, stable deep equality, inclusion/contain, deep property, exact/all/any keys, length, oneOf, empty, numeric comparisons, type, boolean and regex checks are implemented.
Opt-in callback requests support bounded HTTP(S) subrequests, headers, raw bodies, response text/JSON and response assertions; proxy/TLS parity and broader request options remain limited.
Logs are captured locally but not printed by the CLI to avoid accidental secret disclosure.
